newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Former self-styled emperor Bokassa dead - son.
newsitem.headline: Former self-styled emperor Bokassa dead - son.

text.p: Jean-Bedel Bokassa, disgraced self-proclaimed emperor of the Central African Republic, has died, his son Jean Charles said on Monday.
Bokassa, 75, who had been ill with kidney, suspected cerebral and other problems, died of a heart attack on Sunday night at a clinic in the capital Bangui, he added.
Bokassa seized power in 1966. He crowned himself emperor of the diamond-rich but impoverished nation in a lavish ceremony in 1977, only to be ousted in a French-backed coup in 1979.

He lived in exile in Ivory Coast and France but in 1986 he suddenly returned to Central African Republic, where he was sentenced to death for murder and embezzlement after a trial coloured by accusations of infanticide and cannibalism.
The military leader at the time, Andre Kolingba, commuted Bokassa's sentence to life in prison and then freed him in 1993 on the eve of a return to multi-party democracy.
Bokassa returned home to the Central African Republic in mid-October markedly improved, after about two weeks of intensive care in a private clinic in Ivory Coast.
Medical sources in Ivory Coast suggested he might need surgery to remove a brain tumour, but his son said on his return to Bangui that he had simply been been put on kidney dialysis in Abidjan.

Bokassa, who lived quietly in Bangui following his release from jail, had asked President Ange-Felix Patasse for a formal amnesty so that he could stand as a candidate in presidential elections planned for 1999.
